title: Plate Solve Latency by Solver
dataSources: NINA sequences (`nina:sequence`), NINA autofocus runs (`nina:autofocus`), Ekos scheduler and device events (`ekos:scheduler`, `ekos:device`), PHD2 guiding telemetry (`phd2:guide`), plate solves (`platesolve:run`), filter wheel events (`filterwheel:event`), and flat frames (`flatlib:frame`).
app: Astrophotography session telemetry from N.I.N.A., KStars/Ekos, PHD2, plate-solving tools, ASCOM gear, and filter-wheel controllers sent to Splunk HEC via logs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=platesolve:run
| search solve_sec=*
| stats avg(solve_sec) as avg_solve_sec perc90(solve_sec) as p90_solve_sec count as samples by solver_name
| sort 0 - avg_solve_sec
description: Measures plate solve time by solver.
value: Solver latency matters during framing changes and recovery workflows, so it helps to know which backend is dragging.
implementation: Send the relevant duration field for plate solve time to `index=personal` and review both average and p90 latency instead of relying on single examples.
visualization: Table of average and p90 plate solve time.
grandmaExplanation: It blends how long plate solve time usually takes, so slowdowns are obvious instead of anecdotal.
